title: Sore Eye After Recent Surgery

patient.name: Mdm Ang Bee Choo
patient.presenting_complaint: Walk-in with an increasingly painful, red right eye and worsening vision four days after cataract surgery

history.hpc: Mdm Ang had right cataract surgery four days ago and comes in without an appointment. She says: 'After my operation a few days okay, but now my eye more red, more pain and the vision getting worse.' Increasing pain, redness, and falling vision after recent intraocular surgery is a red flag (possible endophthalmitis) and the recent-surgery status is a SNEC triage Section A urgent factor.
history.pmhx: Right cataract surgery 4 days ago. Diabetes, hypertension.
medications: Post-op antibiotic and steroid drops (right eye)
history.social_hx: Lives with daughter who brought her in.

va.right: worse than at the post-op review (e.g. 6/60)

iop.right: to be assessed by the doctor

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: increased redness and discomfort post-op; possible anterior chamber inflammation — for urgent doctor review

investigations.front_line_triage: Recognise that recent intraocular surgery (Section A urgent factor) with increasing pain, redness, and worsening vision is a red flag for a serious post-operative complication (e.g., endophthalmitis). Triage as urgent — same-day assessment / escalate to the doctor — rather than booking a routine appointment.
investigations.va_distance: RE worse than at post-op review, LE 6/9.

diagnosis: A post-operative red flag: increasing pain, redness, and worsening vision after recent cataract surgery, which can indicate a serious complication such as endophthalmitis and must be seen urgently. The PSA competency is recognising the recent-surgery red flag (Section A), triaging it urgently, and escalating rather than queueing routinely.

immediate: Recognise recent intraocular surgery plus increasing pain/redness/worsening vision as a red flag
Treat recent surgery as a SNEC triage Section A urgent factor
Triage as urgent (same-day assessment) and escalate to the doctor promptly
Check VA and compare with the post-op review where available
Do not book a routine future appointment for this presentation
Document the surgery date, symptoms, VA, and the urgent triage outcome
follow_up: Doctor to assess urgently for a post-operative complication (e.g., endophthalmitis)
Ensure the patient is seen the same day and notes follow her
Record the triage outcome on the SNEC triage form
patient_education: Explain that symptoms getting worse after surgery need to be checked quickly
Reassure her she will be seen today rather than given a later appointment
Advise her to continue her drops until the doctor reviews unless told otherwise
Ask her to report any further worsening immediately while waiting

key_points: Establishes the recent cataract surgery and the time since
Identifies the worsening pain, redness, and falling vision
Recognises recent surgery as a key urgent (Section A) factor
Checks VA and compares with the post-op review where possible
Treats the recent-surgery status as a red flag in triage
Assigns urgent (same-day) triage rather than a routine slot
Documents surgery date, symptoms, VA, and triage outcome
Recognises post-op worsening as a red flag for serious complication
Understands endophthalmitis is a sight-threatening possibility
Knows recent surgery elevates triage urgency (Section A)
Knows diagnosis/management is the doctor's role
Avoids booking a routine appointment for this red-flag presentation
Reassures the patient and advises on interim care
